comparison: Perfect alignment on species-specific recommender performance (C23, C47, C82, C83). Both evaluations find this approach well-supported, with reviewers highlighting it as a strength achieving 0.9 ROC AUC. OpenEval notes the contingency on data availability while reviewers emphasize the intermediate approach's maximum performance.

Both address embedding visualizations (C28-C33, C37) but with different conclusions. OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED, noting clear species clustering and taxonomic structure. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting mechanistic features and identifying lack of resistance-associated peak information as a critical weakness.

Strong agreement on transfer learning benefits (C20, C26, C27, C48, C63, C64). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Reviewers praise this as encouraging data integration across locations. OpenEval notes the mechanistic explanations (C63-C64) remain somewhat speculative but finds the experimental design appropriate.

Both affirm the overall contribution and proof-of-concept nature (C50, C72). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED as first large-scale recommender. Editor explicitly validates the work as valuable for computational biologists, microbiologists, and clinicians, confirming the contribution's significance.

Partial overlap on architecture comparisons (C21, C46, C99, C100). Both SUPPORTED. Reviewers note remarkably good performance across embedder combinations and dual network superiority. OpenEval finds systematic comparisons in Figure 2 support claims but notes interpretations (C98-C101) remain somewhat speculative.

Partial overlap on embedder performance (C22, C45, C57). Both SUPPORTED. Reviewers acknowledge ROC AUC scores above 0.8 for global and species-specific evaluations. OpenEval finds Figure 2 and appendix figures directly support these comparative performance claims.

Partial overlap on dual network performance (C24, C49, C58). Both SUPPORTED. Reviewers explicitly affirm consistent performance and dual network superiority. OpenEval notes Table 3 comparisons across 200 species-drug combinations support these claims, with metric-dependent differences clearly documented.

Minimal overlap on C19 (dual network architecture performance). Both SUPPORTED. Reviewers note dual network outperforms single spectrum-drug network. OpenEval finds systematic experimental results in Figure 2 support this claim along with other architecture comparisons.

OpenEval evaluates dataset documentation and preprocessing (C14-C18, C75-C81) as SUPPORTED with comprehensive detail and well-justified temporal split. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.
OpenEval evaluates citations about hospital-specific effects (C34-C36) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate references to prior work and domain knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval marks label quality concerns (C38-C39, C66-C68) as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable concerns but lack of quantitative assessment and explicitly speculative postulations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates practical limitations and negative consequences (C40-C44, C69-C71) as SUPPORTED, noting thoughtful discussion though some inferences remain speculative without empirical validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates metric definitions (C51-C53) as SUPPORTED with clear standard definitions, though notes the clinical interpretation assumption is somewhat simplified. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates training procedures (C89-C93) as SUPPORTED with detailed, standard, and reasonable methodology supporting reproducibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates background and motivation claims (C1-C13) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and context, though notes these are not primary results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
